title: Himachal Pradesh
name: Himachal Pradesh
intro: Himachal Pradesh has had 68 assembly seats since the 1976 order and has 68 today. The state was not divided and its assembly was not interrupted, so the constituencies drawn in 1976 were contested without a break until 2007, when the 2008 order replaced them. Beneath the unchanged total, the redraw was substantial: the hill districts of Kangra and Mandi were reorganised and a number of long-standing names disappeared.
The assembly map Himachal Pradesh used for three decades

map_caveats: The pre-2008 boundaries have been georectified. The source digitisation of the 1976-order map was displaced relative to the 2008-order map; the correction was fitted on the outer boundary of the state, which is unchanged between the two orders, and raises the agreement between the two outlines from an intersection-over-union of 0.95 to 0.97.
Reservation status is taken from the Election Commission's records rather than from the constituency geometry.

Territory lineage is given on two footings, and each seat record states which applies to it. For 64 of the 68 pre-2008 seats the link is derived from the text of the two orders, which describe constituencies in the same vocabulary of tehsils, kanungo circles and patwar circles. For the remainder the successor shown is the one holding the largest share of the old seat's area, inferred from the boundaries alone.
Territory percentages are measured from the mapped boundaries in every case, and are areal shares, not shares of the electorate.
footnotes: Himachal Pradesh's assembly has had 68 elected seats since the 1976 order; the state was not reorganised between the two orders.
Reservation status reflects the category in force at the time of the relevant order, not any later reclassification.
